cards.title: Extreme weather impacts on consumers and insurers in Canada, Dec 2019 to Dec 2025
cards.claim: In the 2024 catastrophe quarter home claims ratios far exceeded auto, then reversed in Q4 2025, showing home results swing with catastrophe timing.

stat.what: Claims ratio (insurance service expenses / insurance revenue), personal property vs auto

cards.relevance: A one-period home ratio near 1.0 is plausibly a cat-year effect shared market-wide, not proof of underpricing.
cards.limit: Claims ratio excludes expenses and is quarterly, not annual; not a combined ratio.

cards.title: Wawanesa P&C profit up 25 per cent (2025 results)
cards.claim: One national insurer reported auto running worse than personal property in 2025 and 2024, the opposite of the book's home-versus-auto gap.

stat.what: Wawanesa undiscounted combined ratio by line

cards.relevance: Shows home is not always the worse line across the market, so the insurer's gap may be company-specific.
cards.limit: Single insurer with its own mix; undiscounted basis.

cards.title: Intact Q3 profit falls as storms hit home cover
cards.claim: Catastrophe losses added 33 points to Intact's Canadian home combined ratio in Q3 2026, and management sees home pricing staying firm.

stat.value: 105.0% personal property combined ratio; 33 cat points

cards.relevance: Confirms a market-wide home deterioration from weather, comparable to the insurer's elevated home ratio.
cards.limit: Trade-press summary of a quarterly release; no rate figure quantified.

cards.title: Catastrophe losses push Definity to Q3 underwriting loss
cards.claim: Definity's home combined ratio jumped from low-80s to above 112 in a year as cat points rose roughly tenfold, while auto stayed near 96.

stat.value: 112.1% vs 83.6% prior year; cat 32.6 pts vs 3.6
stat.what: Definity personal property combined ratio, Q3 2026 vs Q3 2025

cards.relevance: Demonstrates how much of a home loss ratio is volatile catastrophe load rather than base-rate inadequacy.
cards.limit: Quarterly, one insurer, includes cat; article gives no rate actions.

cards.title: Severe weather-related insured losses in Canada exceed $2.4 billion in 2025
cards.claim: Insured weather and wildfire losses in 2016-2025 nearly tripled versus the prior decade, implying a rising structural catastrophe load for home.
cards.relevance: Supports setting a higher, volatility-aware cat load while noting 2025 was a milder year.
cards.limit: National aggregate; says nothing about one insurer's territory mix.

cards.title: Insurance in Canada: What's driving premiums higher?
cards.claim: Homeowner insurance premiums rose about twice as fast as general prices from 2019 to 2025, and faster than auto premiums.

stat.value: +45.0% home vs +21.0% CPI vs +23.9% auto premiums (Dec 2019-Dec 2025)

cards.relevance: Shows the market has been repricing home heavily; a book with flat city premiums may have lagged this.
cards.limit: Consumer price index, not insurer-level written premium or adequacy.

cards.title: Residential construction and repair costs (StatCan 11-627-M)
cards.claim: Residential building construction prices rose far more than routine homeowner repair costs, so replacement-cost exposure grew faster than maintenance inflation.

stat.value: +69.4% construction price index (Q4 2019-Q4 2025); +19.1% maintenance and repair

cards.relevance: Insured values and claim severity likely outran premiums unless sums insured were indexed.
cards.limit: Construction index covers new builds, not insurer repair claims; same page as HP-06.

cards.title: Pressures mounting on home insurance premiums as construction costs soar by 66 percent since 2019
cards.claim: IBC reports rebuilding costs and weather-damaged contents costs climbed sharply since 2019, pushing claims severity up.

stat.value: +24% home replacement cost; +115% personal property claims since 2019

cards.relevance: Severity trend supports a higher claims-to-premium ratio for home than auto.
cards.limit: Late-2024 release; later data showed replacement costs easing; industry advocacy source.

cards.title: Home Insuramap Report 2026 (Ontario, via Insurance-Canada.ca)
cards.claim: Quote data show Ontario city premiums spread widely, with system-backup risk flagged in about a third of postal areas and cited as a main premium driver.

stat.value: Ontario avg $2,235; $1,709 (Newmarket) to $3,322 (Cochrane); backup risk in 32.5% of FSAs
stat.what: Average quoted premium, standard 2,500 sq ft home

cards.relevance: The market prices territory and backup risk with much wider spread than the insurer's 1,110-1,400 range.
cards.limit: Quoted prices with max water coverage for a fixed profile, not written premium; Ontario only.

cards.title: Canada home insurance outlook 2026
cards.claim: Provincial average premiums differ modestly, Quebec sitting below Ontario, and home condition and aging stock are becoming key pricing factors.

stat.value: Quebec $1,284 vs Ontario $1,458 vs national $1,343; Quebec +3.97%

cards.relevance: A Quebec-heavy book with premiums near 1,110-1,400 is not far from market averages, tempering a pure underpricing story.
cards.limit: Broker quote-based averages; no Montreal or Toronto city figure; commercial blog.

cards.title: Montreal flooding lawsuits put spotlight on Canada's overland flood insurance gap
cards.claim: Sewer backup and overland flood are optional endorsements, Quebec sees many flood claims yearly, and high-risk areas face caps, high deductibles or declined coverage.

stat.value: ~25,000 flood claims per year in Quebec; ~$2.5B insured loss in 2024 floods

cards.relevance: Explains why Montreal water frequency can be high and why endorsement, deductible and limit design matter for pricing.
cards.limit: News article citing IBC; no Montreal-versus-Toronto frequency comparison.

cards.title: Water protection in Quebec (Aviva)
cards.claim: Quebec insurers sell water coverage as separate add-ons, with overflow of water bodies requiring the ground water and sewer endorsement.
cards.relevance: Shows water risk is priced through modular endorsements, so base premiums by city may understate water exposure.
cards.limit: Product page with no prices, limits or deductibles.

cards.title: Intact and Definity put Q3 catastrophe losses at $850 million combined
cards.claim: Water damage, including basement flooding in Ontario and Quebec storms, drove most of the Q3 2026 home catastrophe losses at two large insurers.

stat.value: ~$850M combined cat; $491M CatIQ for Jun 30-Jul 3 ON/QC storms

cards.relevance: Water losses hit Ontario as well as Quebec this year, so a Montreal-only frequency gap may be partly event noise.
cards.limit: Event-driven quarter; no frequency by city.

cards.title: Insights into the impact of extreme weather trends on homeowners insurance profitability
cards.claim: Home claims ratios stayed above 50% since 2020 but did not exceed 80% nationally, while regional spikes like PEI reached about 393% in one hurricane year.
cards.relevance: Regional and small-book loss ratios are extremely volatile, so tier-level ratios like 1.29 vs 0.98 may be noise.
cards.limit: Claims ratio excludes expenses; no auto ratio given.
